task: Make the Codex metrics processor record apply_patch custom tool calls (one shared per-call patch parse with file operations, sub-agent rollouts, failure status, no double count on resume) and compute Codex active duration from turn start/end records.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches CodexMetricsProcessor (custom_tool_call / custom_tool_call_output pairing, fileOperations, real toolStatus), the apply_patch parser in codex-metrics-extractor (refactored into a shared per-call parse that also feeds ParsedSession.metrics via codex.session), a new turn-based active-duration writer (task_started/task_complete) that interacts with SessionStore and the shared SessionEnd path in hook.ts, plus the onSessionEnd / incremental-sync callers. 3-4 components in the Codex plugin plus core session store, with a new shared parsing abstraction.

Closest patterns: pi saveActiveDurationMs (processor-written activeDurationMs) and opencode/pi per-call fileOperations on success only. They cover the shape but not the Codex-specific parts: patch result from patch_apply_end (unread anywhere today), Add->write mapping change that alters native analytics, double-count risk between a processor-written activeDurationMs and hook.ts accumulateActiveDuration, resume dedupe for turns, and an external version-dependent rollout format. Base M, bumped to L because the AC enumerate edge cases (interrupted/open turns, idle gaps, no turns, failed patches, pending results, resume) and no existing Codex test template covers patch parsing, custom tool calls or active duration.

Estimated 5-7 modified files (codex.metrics-processor.ts, codex-metrics-extractor.ts, codex.session.ts, codex-message-types.ts, possibly codex.plugin.ts, existing processor and extractor tests) and 1-2 new (shared patch parse / active-duration helper and its test) across codex/session, codex/session/processors and codex/__tests__. Calibration: consistent with bundled M example epmcdme-10202 (5 files, patterns available); clearly smaller than project L example profile-provider-decoupling (14 files, data migration).
